title: commit-burst-swap-hc-pricing-experiment-nov2025
content:
Sheet: Commit-to-Burst Swap + Convertible HC Pool (working model)

Purpose: quick-turn budgeting and sensitivity model that connects reserved capacity commitments, burst pool economics, and a small convertible headcount bucket that can be re-allocated to ops during price stress. Designed to produce a set of triggers and short SOPs for pricing moves and hiring pauses.

SUMMARY TABLE (scenario rows)
Columns: Scenario | Avg tokens/mo (M) | Hosted revenue/mo ($k) | Infra cost/mo ($k) | Staff cost/mo ($k) | Reserved commit ($k/mo) | Burst overage ($k/mo) | Net contribution/mo ($k) | HC deployed (FTE) | Convertible HC (FTE)
Base | 4,200 | 1,260 | 420 | 350 | 80 | 50 | 360 | 48 | 6
Upside | 6,500 | 1,950 | 650 | 420 | 80 | 120 | 680 | 60 | 4
Downside | 2,800 | 840 | 300 | 300 | 80 | 10 | 150 | 40 | 8

Key formulas (text):
- Hosted revenue/mo = tokens_million * price_per_1M_tokens ($300 assumed base)
- Infra cost/mo = tokens_million * infra_cost_per_1M ($100 base, adjusted by GPU mix)
- Staff cost/mo = FTE_count * avg_loaded_comp ($7.3k/mo) prorated by team mix (ops/eng/sales)
- Net contribution = hosted_revenue - infra_cost - staff_cost - reserved_commit - burst_overage

Assumptions (explicit):
- Price per 1M tokens: Base = $300; experiment sweep = [$240, $270, $300, $330, $360]
- Elasticity rule (working hypothesis): each -10% price = +18% token volume (front-loaded in 6 weeks), +10% price = -12% volume. This is intentionally aggressive; treat as prior for sensitivity not forecast.
- Reserved commit is fixed via contracts and amortized into month. Burst overage is variable and measured at actual usage.
- Convertible HC pool = 6 FTEs in Base that can be redeployed from BD/marketing into ops within 4–6 weeks in a stress scenario.
- Infra cost composition: 65% GPU compute, 20% storage/network, 15% cloud overhead and reserved amortization.

PRICE SWEEP SENSITIVITY (table excerpt):
Columns: Price per 1M | Expected tokens (M) | Revenue ($k) | Infra cost ($k) | Net contribution delta vs base ($k) | Notes
$240 (-20%) | 5,800 (+38%) | 1,392 | 580 | +2.0k approx | heavy upper bound on volume growth; reserves hit earlier
$270 (-10%) | 4,956 (+18%) | 1,487 | 496 | +1.1k | positive leverage; watch latency tiering
$300 (base) | 4,200 | 1,260 | 420 | 0 baseline |
$330 (+10%) | 3,696 (-12%) | 1,109 | 370 | -220 | revenue-contraction risk vs fixed staff
$360 (+20%) | 3,360 (-20%) | 1,008 | 336 | -500 | may preserve margin per-token but reduces throughput and accelerates churn in SMB segment

Observations from sweep: margin elasticity mostly driven by infra (scale) and staff fixed costs. If volume elasticity is >~+25% for -20% price we get upside; otherwise margin compresses.

HEADCOUNT PHASING (notes + quick calendar):
- Q4 hiring freeze triggers: if 3-month rolling net contribution drops > 25% vs forecast -> freeze convertible hires and pause 50% of open reqs. Owner: People Ops + Finance.
- Convertible HC redeploy protocol: operations lead to submit redeploy request ticket (ops-redeploy/JIRA) -> finance signoff (48h) -> people ops executes redeploy payroll re-coding (effective within 4 weeks).
- Backfill rule: only refill convertible bucket after 2 consecutive months of net contribution recovery > 10%.

RESERVE & BURST PLAY (operational economics):
- Commit-to-burst swap concept: reassign up to 15% of reserved dollars from GPU reserve into a burst credit pool at quarter boundary to buy short-term capacity at spot. Net effect: lower fixed reserved amortization, higher variable cost exposure.
- When to execute: if expected next-quarter token variance > 30% (via internal traffic forecast models) and price elasticity implies strong volume upside, run swap.
- Trigger test: run a simulated swap on a 6-week window with price at -10%: if burst utilization < 40% and marginal infra cost <= $110 per 1M tokens, approve.

RISK TABLE (short bullets):
- Demand overestimate: convertible HC redeployed poorly -> quality/regression issues in ops. Mitigation: 2-week cross-training, maintain 2-person coverage minimum on core functions.
- Contract cliffs: multi-quarter reserved commitments misaligned with new price tiers -> renegotiate mid-term; legal to review.
- Elasticity assumption wrong: run small AB price experiments with 1–5% of traffic before sweeping to whole book.

EXPERIMENTATION PLAN (30–90 day cadence):
1) Small AB price test: target 5% of paying customers, -10% price for 6 weeks; measure activation, next-month retention.
2) Convert 3 FTEs from BD into ops for 6 weeks as a tactical support pilot; measure ops throughput and incident MTTR impact.
3) Run a mock commit-to-burst swap in the infra billing sandbox (Finance + Cloud ops) to estimate true marginal infra cost.

METRICS TO TRACK (dashboard):
- Effective unit margin per 1M tokens (revenue - infra - direct staff)
- Burst utilization % of available credits (daily)
- Convertible HC redeploy velocity (time from request to active)
- 90-day revenue velocity by cohort (price-treated vs control)

OPEN QUESTIONS / DECISIONS NEEDED:
- Legal: can we add a flexible reserve clause into new enterprise contracts for small swap capacity? (assigned to Legal, due 2025-12-01)
- Product: can we gate price AB tests by region to limit fallout on multi-region customers? (Product owner: Priya Gupta)
- Infra: can ops provision an isolated burst pool on-demand under 24h? (Ops ticket PR-321)

ACTION ITEMS (immediate):
- Finance to build a daily marginal infra cost feed for the model (owner: Maya) - due 2025-11-21
- Run AB price test design doc and recruit cohorts (owner: Growth - Omar) - due 2025-11-28
- People Ops to draft redeploy payroll workflow (owner: Lucas) - due 2025-12-05

NOTES / CONTEXT:
- This is purposely a working sheet: treat numbers as inputs to an experiment pipeline, not firm guidance to sales.
- Related reading: pricing elasticity primer (Confluence link in linked_artifacts), previous Q2 commit-swap trial deck (see FIN-deck Q2 2025).

VERSION HISTORY (short):
- 2025-11-14 created (initial stitch of commit/burst ideas)
- 2025-12-03 updated with early infra cost breakdown from cloud ops
- 2026-02-27 updated price sweep using February traffic telemetry and revised elasticity priors

End of sheet.
